name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Hawaii's urban Honolulu district leans Democratic by 13 points on partisanship
Incumbent Ed Case is running with a $1.1 million warhead and $600K on hand
Republican Adriel Lam has no reported fundraising or outside support
Polymarket prices Case's win probability at 96%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Case: a +13 Democratic district, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a little-known, unfunded challenger. Markets agree, pricing the race at 96% Democratic, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-implied margin of roughly 22 points.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or polling showing Lam within single digits would warrant revisiting, though nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ed Case, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term representing urban Honolulu in a district that voted 13 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with about $1.1 million raised and $600,000 on hand, while Republican Adriel Lam reports no fundraising and no outside spending on either side. A Green and an independent candidate also appear on the ballot but lack resources.

Prediction markets give Case roughly a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on partisanship, incumbency, and the money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Case victory in the low-twenties margin range.
